sentences.text: The genus Plesiolophus contains only one species, P. warnerensis, known from a partial skull.
This fossil material represents the first diagnostic remains of an adult lambeosaurine from the Oldman Formation.
The fossil remains were discovered by Wendy Sloboda near Warner, Alberta, Canada.
The holotype specimen — the specimen the species is based on — is housed at the Royal Tyrrell Museum of Palaeontology under the accession number TMP 2016.023.0039.
Plesiolophus is classified within the class Ornithischia, belongs to the family Hadrosauridae, and its parent group is the tribe Parasaurolophini.
Phylogenetic analysis places it as the basalmost member of an exclusively North American clade within Parasaurolophini.
Plesiolophus lived during the Late Cretaceous period, specifically the Campanian age, between 83.6 and 72.2 million years ago.
Its fossils come from the Oldman Formation, which lies beneath the Dinosaur Park Formation.
